main_body: Stone forge: a chimney hood on top of a furnace front with a fire opening, a grate ledge and a stone base, all drawn flat-on
top_band: rows 1-3 L=137 (#828a95) sit under a dark outline at row 0. This reads as the chimney's inner face panel, not a horizontal surface. Only a thin light line at row 5 (L=206) acts as a ledge.
evidence: The whole forge is a straight front view. The chimney is a framed panel, the fire opening is a flat black strip filled with flames painted on the face, and the grate ledge at row 25 is a 1px light line. No top surface is seen from above: the chimney and hood have no visible cap or slope, and the stone block courses are all vertical. The fire opening is not set into the front with an inner shadow. This matches the red front-elevation guide.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 16 distinct colours against 185 and 66 in the references. The stone ramp has about 4-5 flat steps with little per-stone shading or speckle. The dark edge pixels are 81% neutral, against 7-9% in the references, so the outline is the uniform dark sticker line rather than a tinted material tone. The fire is the richest area, but the stone and hood are repeated blocks of 2-3 greys. Median colours per tile (15) match the references, but the very low total palette and neutral outline make it thinner and more sticker-like than them.
